sentences.text: Fossils of Pseudomegachasma have been found in Cretaceous rock layers in Russia and the United States. This animal was a member of the class Chondrichthyes, which includes cartilaginous fish like sharks and rays.
Pseudomegachasma is the only known planktivorous member of the Odontaspididae family and the oldest known planktivorous elasmobranch.
The type species of the genus Pseudomegachasma is Pseudomegachasma casei, which serves as the primary reference for the group.
Scientists have recorded 12 fossil occurrences of this species in the Paleobiology Database.
Researchers suggest that Pseudomegachasma likely evolved from its close relative, the carnivorous shark Johnlongia.
Taxonomically, Pseudomegachasma belongs to the subfamily Johnlonginae within the family Odontaspididae.
Pseudomegachasma lived during the Albian to Turonian stages, approximately 106.3 to 89.8 million years ago.
